parts: how do i open a url in windows 10 command-line? (CMD or powershell)

To open a URL from the Windows Command Prompt (CMD) or PowerShell, you can use the following commands:

1. In CMD:
   ```
   start https://www.example.com
   ```
   
2. In PowerShell:
   ```
   Start-Process "https://www.example.com"
   ```

Both commands will launch the default web browser and navigate to the specified URL.

will running 
```
start "cataclysmbnteam/Cataclysm-BN/issues/new?labels=bug&template=bug_report.yml&versions-and-configuration=-%20OS%3A%20Windows%0A%20%20%20%20-%20OS%20Version%3A%2010.0%202009%0A-%20Game%20Version%3A%20e01f656%20%5B64-bit%5D%0A-%20Graphics%20Version%3A%20Tiles%0A-%20Game%20Language%3A%20English%20%5Ben_US%5D%0A-%20Mods%20loaded%3A%20%5B%0A%20%20%20%20Bright%20Nights%20%5Bbn%5D%0A%5D%0A"
```
in CMD.exe open correct url?

No, running that command in CMD.exe will not open the correct URL. The reason is that the `start` command in CMD.exe treats the first argument in quotes as the title for the new Command Prompt window that gets opened.

You can get around this by providing an empty title argument like this:

```cmd
start "" "cataclysmbnteam/Cataclysm-BN/issues/new?labels=bug&template=bug_report.yml&versions-and-configuration=-%20OS%3A%20Windows%0A%20%20%20%20-%20OS%20Version%3A%2010.0%202009%0A-%20Game%20Version%3A%20e01f656%20%5B64-bit%5D%0A-%20Graphics%20Version%3A%20Tiles%0A-%20Game%20Language%3A%20English%20%5Ben_US%5D%0A-%20Mods%20loaded%3A%20%5B%0A%20%20%20%20Bright%20Nights%20%5Bbn%5D%0A%5D%0A"
```

However, this command will still fail because the URL is incomplete (it lacks the `https://` prefix and the domain name).

A complete and correct command should look something like this:

```cmd
start "" "https://github.com/cataclysmbnteam/Cataclysm-BN/issues/new?labels=bug&template=bug_report.yml&versions-and-configuration=-%20OS%3A%20Windows%0A%20%20%20%20-%20OS%20Version%3A%2010.0%202009%0A-%20Game%20Version%3A%20e01f656%20%5B64-bit%5D%0A-%20Graphics%20Version%3A%20Tiles%0A-%20Game%20Language%3A%20English%20%5Ben_US%5D%0A-%20Mods%20loaded%3A%20%5B%0A%20%20%20%20Bright%20Nights%20%5Bbn%5D%0A%5D%0A"
```

The issue is likely in the `open_url` function's handling for Windows. The code for `_WIN64` should not be `"start"` but `"start \"\""` to handle the argument correctly. Here's the modified portion of your `open_url` function:

```cpp
#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(_WIN64)
    executable = "start \"\"";
```

This change makes sure that `start` does not mistake your URL for the title of the window.

Additionally, please ensure that the `#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(_WIN64)` is correct based on your build target, as `_WIN32` will also be defined for 64-bit builds. So having separate blocks for `_WIN32` and `_WIN64` may not behave as expected. Just having one block to handle Windows should be enough.
